583 U.S. 71.source: United States Reports, U.S. Government Publishing Office

584 U.S. 1.name: Marinello v. United States
584 U.S. 1.source: Supreme Court of the United States
584 U.S. 1.excerpt: To convict a defendant under 26 U. S. C. §7212(a)—which forbids “corruptly or by force or threats of force . . . obstruct[ing] or imped[ing], or endeavor[ing] to obstruct or impede, the due administration of [the Internal Revenue Code]”—the Government must prove the defendant was aware of a pending tax-related proceeding, such as a particular investigation or audit, or could reasonably foresee that such a proceeding would commence.

584 U.S. 100.name: Kisela v. Hughes
584 U.S. 100.source: Supreme Court of the United States
584 U.S. 100.excerpt: Petitioner police officer is entitled to qualified immunity here, where his actions did not violate clearly established statutory or constitutional rights of which a reasonable person would have known.

584 U.S. 122.name: Wilson v. Sellers
584 U.S. 122.source: Supreme Court of the United States
584 U.S. 122.excerpt: A federal habeas court reviewing an unexplained state-court decision on the merits should “look through” that decision to the last related state-court decision that provides a relevant rationale and presume that the unexplained decision adopted the same reasoning; the State may rebut the presumption by showing that the unexplained decision most likely relied on different grounds than the reasoned decision below.

584 U.S. 148.name: Sessions v. Dimaya
584 U.S. 148.source: Supreme Court of the United States
584 U.S. 148.excerpt: The Ninth Circuit’s judgment—that 18 U. S. C. §16(b), which defines violent felony for purposes of the Immigration and Nationality Act’s removal provisions, is unconstitutionally vague—is affirmed.

584 U.S. 236.name: United States v. Microsoft Corp.
584 U.S. 236.source: Supreme Court of the United States
584 U.S. 236.excerpt: The Second Circuit’s judgment is vacated, and the case is remanded with instructions to dismiss the case as moot.

584 U.S. 241.name: Jesner v. Arab Bank, PLC
584 U.S. 241.source: Supreme Court of the United States
584 U.S. 241.excerpt: The Second Circuit’s judgment—that foreign corporations may not be defendants in suits brought under the Alien Tort Statute—is affirmed.

584 U.S. 28.name: Ayestas v. Davis
584 U.S. 28.source: Supreme Court of the United States
584 U.S. 28.excerpt: The District Court’s denial of petitioner’s request for funding for “reasonably necessary” services of experts, investigators, and the like, 18 U. S. C. §3599(f), to develop his claim that both his trial and state habeas counsel were ineffective was a judicial decision subject to appellate review under the standard jurisdictional provisions; the Fifth Circuit did not apply the correct legal standard in affirming the denial of that request.

584 U.S. 325.name: Oil States Energy Services, LLC v. Greene’s Energy Group, LLC
584 U.S. 325.source: Supreme Court of the United States
584 U.S. 325.excerpt: Inter partes review—which authorizes the United States Patent and Trademark Office to reconsider and cancel an already-issued patent claim, see 35 U. S. C. §§311–319—does not violate Article III or the Seventh Amendment of the Constitution.

584 U.S. 357.name: SAS Institute Inc. v. Iancu
584 U.S. 357.source: Supreme Court of the United States
584 U.S. 357.excerpt: When the United States Patent and Trademark Office institutes an inter partes review to reconsider an already-issued patent claim, see 35 U. S. C. §§311–319, it must decide the patentability of all of the claims the petitioner has challenged.

584 U.S. 381.name: United States v. Sanchez-Gomez
584 U.S. 381.source: Supreme Court of the United States
584 U.S. 381.excerpt: Respondents’ appeals challenging the use of full restraints during nonjury pretrial proceedings became moot when their underlying criminal cases came to an end before the Ninth Circuit could render its decision.

584 U.S. 395.name: Byrd v. United States
584 U.S. 395.source: Supreme Court of the United States
584 U.S. 395.excerpt: The mere fact that a driver in lawful possession or control of a rental car is not listed on the rental agreement will not defeat his or her otherwise reasonable expectation of privacy protected by the Fourth Amendment.

584 U.S. 414.name: McCoy v. Louisiana
584 U.S. 414.source: Supreme Court of the United States
584 U.S. 414.excerpt: The Sixth Amendment guarantees a defendant the right to choose the objective of his defense and to insist that his counsel refrain from admitting guilt, even when counsel’s experienced-based view is that confessing guilt offers the defendant the best chance to avoid the death penalty.

584 U.S. 440.name: Dahda v. United States
584 U.S. 440.source: Supreme Court of the United States
584 U.S. 440.excerpt: Wiretap orders authorized by a judge for the District of Kansas in the Government’s investigation of a suspected Kansas drug distribution ring were not facially insufficient, since they were not lacking any information that the wiretap statute required them to include and since the challenged language authorizing interception outside the court’s territorial jurisdiction was surplus.

584 U.S. 453.name: Murphy v. National Collegiate Athletic Assn.
584 U.S. 453.source: Supreme Court of the United States
584 U.S. 453.excerpt: Professional and Amateur Sports Protection Act (PASPA) provisions that prohibit state authorization and licensing of sports gambling schemes, see 28 U. S. C. §3702(1), violate the Constitution’s anticommandeering rule; no other PASPA provisions are severable from the provisions at issue.

584 U.S. 497.name: Epic Systems Corp. v. Lewis
584 U.S. 497.source: Supreme Court of the United States
584 U.S. 497.excerpt: Congress has instructed in the Federal Arbitration Act that arbitration agreements providing for individualized proceedings must be enforced, and neither the Arbitration Act’s saving clause nor the National Labor Relations Act suggests otherwise.

584 U.S. 554.name: Upper Skagit Tribe v. Lundgren
584 U.S. 554.source: Supreme Court of the United States
584 U.S. 554.excerpt: County of Yakima v. Confederated Tribes and Bands of Yakima Nation, 502 U. S. 251, addressed only a question of statutory interpretation of the Indian General Allotment Act of 1887, not the question whether Indian tribes have sovereign immunity in in rem lawsuits.

584 U.S. 586.name: Collins v. Virginia
584 U.S. 586.source: Supreme Court of the United States
584 U.S. 586.excerpt: The Fourth Amendment’s automobile exception does not permit the warrantless entry of a home or its curtilage in order to search a vehicle therein.

584 U.S. 59.name: Hall v. Hall
584 U.S. 59.source: Supreme Court of the United States
584 U.S. 59.excerpt: When one of several cases consolidated under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 42(a) is finally decided, that decision confers upon the losing party the immediate right to appeal, regardless of whether any of the other consolidated cases remain pending.

584 U.S. 617.name: Masterpiece Cakeshop, Ltd. v. Colorado Civil Rights Comm’n
584 U.S. 617.source: Supreme Court of the United States
584 U.S. 617.excerpt: The Colorado Civil Rights Commission’s actions in assessing a cakeshop owner’s reasons for declining to make a cake for a same-sex couple’s wedding celebration violated the Free Exercise Clause.

584 U.S. 675.name: Hughes v. United States
584 U.S. 675.source: Supreme Court of the United States
584 U.S. 675.excerpt: A Federal Rule of Criminal Procedure 11(c)(1)(C) plea agreement is “based on” the defendant’s Federal Sentencing Guidelines range so long as that range was part of the framework the district court relied on in imposing the sentence or accepting the agreement; thus, Hughes may seek a sentencing reduction under 18 U. S. C. §3582(c)(2).

584 U.S. 700.name: Koons v. United States
584 U.S. 700.source: Supreme Court of the United States
584 U.S. 700.excerpt: Petitioners do not qualify for sentence reductions under 18 U. S. C. §3582(c)(2) because their sentences were not “based on” their lowered Federal Sentencing Guidelines ranges but, instead, were “based on” their mandatory minimums and their substantial assistance to the Government.

584 U.S. 709.name: Lamar, Archer & Cofrin, LLP v. Appling
584 U.S. 709.source: Supreme Court of the United States
584 U.S. 709.excerpt: Single-asset statements qualify as “statement[s] respecting the debtor’s . . . financial condition” for purposes of Bankruptcy Code §523(a)(2)’s exceptions to discharge; where, as here, a single-asset statement is not in writing, the associated debt may be discharged.

584 U.S. 726.name: Azar v. Garza
584 U.S. 726.source: Supreme Court of the United States
584 U.S. 726.excerpt: The D. C. Circuit’s judgment is vacated, and the case is remanded with instructions to dismiss the individual claim for injunctive relief as moot.

584 U.S. 756.name: Husted v. A. Philip Randolph Institute
584 U.S. 756.source: Supreme Court of the United States
584 U.S. 756.excerpt: The process that Ohio uses to remove voters on change-of-residence grounds does not violate the National Voter Registration Act.

584 U.S. 79.name: Encino Motorcars, LLC v. Navarro
584 U.S. 79.source: Supreme Court of the United States
584 U.S. 79.excerpt: Because service advisors at car dealerships are “salesm[e]n . . . primarily engaged in . . . servicing automobiles,” 29 U. S. C. §213(b)(10)(A), they are exempt from the Fair Labor Standards Act’s overtime-pay requirement.

584 U.S. 811.name: Sveen v. Melin
584 U.S. 811.source: Supreme Court of the United States
584 U.S. 811.excerpt: The retroactive application of Minnesota’s revocation-on-divorce statute—which automatically nullifies an ex-spouse’s beneficiary designation on a life-insurance policy or other will substitute—does not violate the Contracts Clause.

585 U.S. 1.name: Minnesota Voters Alliance v. Mansky
585 U.S. 1.source: Supreme Court of the United States
585 U.S. 1.excerpt: Minnesota’s ban on political apparel at polling places violates the First Amendment’s Free Speech Clause.

585 U.S. 109.name: Chavez-Meza v. United States
585 U.S. 109.source: Supreme Court of the United States
585 U.S. 109.excerpt: Because the record in this case demonstrates that the judge had a reasoned basis for his decision, the judge’s explanation for reducing, under 18 U. S. C. §3582(c)(2), petitioner’s sentence to the middle rather than the bottom of the amended Federal Guidelines range was adequate.

585 U.S. 129.name: Rosales-Mireles v. United States
585 U.S. 129.source: Supreme Court of the United States
585 U.S. 129.excerpt: A miscalculation of a Federal Guidelines sentencing range that has been determined to be plain and to affect a defendant’s substantial rights calls for a court of appeals to exercise its discretion under Federal Rule of Criminal Procedure 52(b) to vacate the defendant’s sentence in the ordinary case.

585 U.S. 155.name: Benisek v. Lamone
585 U.S. 155.source: Supreme Court of the United States
585 U.S. 155.excerpt: Because the balance of equities and the public interest tilt against the preliminary injunction motion of plaintiffs claiming that a Maryland congressional district was gerrymandered to retaliate against them for their political views, the District Court did not abuse its discretion in denying the motion.

585 U.S. 162.name: South Dakota v. Wayfair, Inc.
585 U.S. 162.source: Supreme Court of the United States
585 U.S. 162.excerpt: Quill Corp. v. North Dakota, 504 U. S. 298, and National Bellas Hess, Inc. v. Department of Revenue of Ill., 386 U. S. 753—which held that a State cannot require an out-of-state seller with no physical presence in the State to collect and remit sales taxes on goods the seller ships to consumers in the State—are overruled.

585 U.S. 198.name: Pereira v. Sessions
585 U.S. 198.source: Supreme Court of the United States
585 U.S. 198.excerpt: A putative notice sent to a nonpermanent resident to appear at a removal proceeding that fails to designate a specific time or place for that proceeding does not end the continuous residence period calculation necessary for possible cancellation of the individual’s removal.

585 U.S. 237.name: Lucia v. SEC
585 U.S. 237.source: Supreme Court of the United States
585 U.S. 237.excerpt: Securities and Exchange Commission administrative law judges are “Officers of the United States,” subject to the Appointments Clause.

585 U.S. 274.name: Wisconsin Central Ltd. v. United States
585 U.S. 274.source: Supreme Court of the United States
585 U.S. 274.excerpt: Employee stock options are not taxable “compensation” under the Railroad Retirement Tax Act of 1937.

585 U.S. 296.name: Carpenter v. United States
585 U.S. 296.source: Supreme Court of the United States
585 U.S. 296.excerpt: The Government’s acquisition of Carpenter’s cell-site records from his wireless carriers was a Fourth Amendment search; and the Government did not obtain a warrant supported by probable cause before acquiring those records.

585 U.S. 33.name: Animal Science Products, Inc. v. Hebei Welcome Pharmaceutical Co.
585 U.S. 33.source: Supreme Court of the United States
585 U.S. 33.excerpt: A federal court determining foreign law under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 44.1 should accord respectful consideration to a foreign government’s submission, but the court is not bound to accord conclusive effect to the foreign government’s statements.

585 U.S. 407.name: WesternGeco LLC v. ION Geophysical Corp.
585 U.S. 407.source: Supreme Court of the United States
585 U.S. 407.excerpt: The focus of the Patent Act’s general damages provision, 35 U. S. C. §284, in a case involving infringement under §271(f)(2) is on the act of exporting components from the United States; therefore, WesternGeco’s award for lost profits was a permissible domestic application of §284, not an extraterritorial one.

585 U.S. 427.name: Ortiz v. United States
585 U.S. 427.source: Supreme Court of the United States
585 U.S. 427.excerpt: Military Judge Mitchell’s simultaneous service on an Air Force appeals court and the Court of Military Commission Review violated neither 10 U. S. C. §973(b)(2)(A) nor the Appointments Clause.

585 U.S. 48.name: Gill v. Whitford
585 U.S. 48.source: Supreme Court of the United States
585 U.S. 48.excerpt: Plaintiffs—Wisconsin Democratic voters who rested their claim of unconstitutional partisan gerrymandering on statewide injury—have failed to demonstrate Article III standing.

585 U.S. 493.name: Currier v. Virginia
585 U.S. 493.source: Supreme Court of the United States
585 U.S. 493.excerpt: Because Currier consented to a severance of the multiple charges against him, his second trial and resulting conviction, following an acquittal at his first trial, did not violate the Double Jeopardy Clause.

585 U.S. 529.name: Ohio v. American Express Co.
585 U.S. 529.source: Supreme Court of the United States
585 U.S. 529.excerpt: American Express’ antisteering provisions in its merchant contracts—which prohibit merchants from avoiding fees by discouraging customers’ American Express card use at the point of sale—do not violate federal antitrust law.

585 U.S. 579.name: Abbott v. Perez
585 U.S. 579.source: Supreme Court of the United States
585 U.S. 579.excerpt: The District Court disregarded the presumption of legislative good faith and improperly reversed the burden of proof when it required the State to show a lack of discriminatory intent in adopting new districting plans; one of the challenged State House districts is an impermissible racial gerrymander.

585 U.S. 667.name: Trump v. Hawaii
585 U.S. 667.source: Supreme Court of the United States
585 U.S. 667.excerpt: The President has lawfully exercised the broad discretion granted to him under 8 U. S. C. §1182(f) to suspend the entry of aliens into the United States; respondents have not demonstrated a likelihood of success on the merits of their claim that Presidential Proclamation No. 9645 violates the Establishment Clause.

585 U.S. 755.name: National Institute of Family and Life Advocates v. Becerra
585 U.S. 755.source: Supreme Court of the United States
585 U.S. 755.excerpt: Petitioners are likely to succeed on their claim that the California Reproductive Freedom, Accountability, Comprehensive Care, and Transparency Act (FACT Act) violates the First Amendment.

585 U.S. 87.name: Lozman v. Riviera Beach
585 U.S. 87.source: Supreme Court of the United States
585 U.S. 87.excerpt: The existence of probable cause for Lozman’s arrest for disrupting a city council meeting does not bar his First Amendment retaliatory arrest claim under the circumstances of this case.

585 U.S. 878.name: Janus v. State, County, and Municipal Employees
585 U.S. 878.source: Supreme Court of the United States
585 U.S. 878.excerpt: The State of Illinois’ extraction of agency fees from nonconsenting public-sector employees violates the First Amendment; Abood v. Detroit Bd. of Ed., 431 U. S. 209, which concluded otherwise, is overruled.

585 U.S. 957.name: Sause v. Bauer
585 U.S. 957.source: Supreme Court of the United States
585 U.S. 957.excerpt: The Tenth Circuit erred in holding that police officers were entitled to qualified immunity without considering the ground on which the officers were present in petitioner’s home and the nature of any legitimate law enforcement interests that might have justified their order that petitioner stop praying at the specific time in question.

585 U.S. 961.name: Sexton v. Beaudreaux
585 U.S. 961.source: Supreme Court of the United States
585 U.S. 961.excerpt: The Ninth Circuit erred in reversing a denial of federal habeas relief on the ground that the state court had unreasonably rejected respondent’s ineffective-assistance-of-counsel claim.

585 U.S. 969.name: North Carolina v. Covington
585 U.S. 969.source: Supreme Court of the United States
585 U.S. 969.excerpt: The District Court’s order is affirmed insofar as it provided a court-drawn remedy for Senate Districts 21 and 28 and House Districts 21 and 57 and reversed as to the court’s actions concerning the legislature’s redrawing of House districts in Wake and Mecklenburg Counties.

586 U.S. 105.name: New Prime Inc. v. Oliveira
586 U.S. 105.source: Supreme Court of the United States
586 U.S. 105.excerpt: A court should determine whether the Federal Arbitration Act’s §1 exclusion for disputes involving the “contracts of employment” of certain transportation workers applies before ordering arbitration; here, truck driver Oliveira’s independent contractor operating agreement with New Prime falls within that exception.

586 U.S. 123.name: Helsinn Healthcare S. A. v. Teva Pharmaceuticals USA, Inc.
586 U.S. 123.source: Supreme Court of the United States
586 U.S. 123.excerpt: The sale of an invention to a third party who is obligated to keep the invention confidential may place the invention “on sale” for purposes of the Leahy-Smith America Invents Act, which bars a person from receiving a patent on an invention that was “in public use, on sale, or otherwise available to the public before the effective filing date of the claimed invention,” 35 U. S. C. §102(a)(1).

586 U.S. 133.name: Moore v. Texas
586 U.S. 133.source: Supreme Court of the United States
586 U.S. 133.excerpt: The Texas Court of Criminal Appeals’ redetermination that Moore does not have an intellectual disability and is thus eligible for the death penalty is inconsistent with Moore v. Texas, 581 U. S. ___.

586 U.S. 146.name: Timbs v. Indiana
586 U.S. 146.source: Supreme Court of the United States
586 U.S. 146.excerpt: The Eighth Amendment’s Excessive Fines Clause is an incorporated protection applicable to the States under the Fourteenth Amendment’s Due Process Clause.

586 U.S. 171.name: Dawson v. Steager
586 U.S. 171.source: Supreme Court of the United States
586 U.S. 171.excerpt: By taxing the federal pension benefits of U. S. Marshals Service retiree Dawson, while exempting from taxation the pension benefits of certain state and local law enforcement officers, West Virginia unlawfully discriminates against Mr. Dawson as 4 U. S. C. §111 forbids.

586 U.S. 181.name: Yovino v. Rizo
586 U.S. 181.source: Supreme Court of the United States
586 U.S. 181.excerpt: The Ninth Circuit erred when it counted as a member of the majority a judge who died before the court’s opinion in this case was filed.

586 U.S. 188.name: Nutraceutical Corp. v. Lambert
586 U.S. 188.source: Supreme Court of the United States
586 U.S. 188.excerpt: Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 23(f), which establishes a 14-day deadline to seek permission to appeal an order granting or denying class certification, is not subject to equitable tolling.

586 U.S. 199.name: Jam v. International Finance Corp.
586 U.S. 199.source: Supreme Court of the United States
586 U.S. 199.excerpt: The International Organizations Immunities Act of 1945 affords international organizations the same immunity from suit that foreign governments enjoy today under the Foreign Sovereign Immunities Act of 1976.

586 U.S. 232.name: Garza v. Idaho
586 U.S. 232.source: Supreme Court of the United States
586 U.S. 232.excerpt: The presumption of prejudice for Sixth Amendment purposes recognized in Roe v. Flores-Ortega, 528 U. S. 470, applies regardless of whether a defendant has signed an appeal waiver.

586 U.S. 265.name: Madison v. Alabama
586 U.S. 265.source: Supreme Court of the United States
586 U.S. 265.excerpt: The Eighth Amendment may permit executing a prisoner even if he cannot remember committing his crime but it may prohibit executing a prisoner who suffers from dementia or another disorder rather than psychotic delusions.

586 U.S. 296.name: Fourth Estate Pub. Benefit Corp. v. Wall-Street.com
586 U.S. 296.source: Supreme Court of the United States
586 U.S. 296.excerpt: Registration occurs, and a copyright claimant may commence an infringement suit, when the Copyright Office registers a copyright.

586 U.S. 310.name: BNSF R. Co. v. Loos
586 U.S. 310.source: Supreme Court of the United States
586 U.S. 310.excerpt: A railroad’s payment to an employee for working time lost due to an on-the-job injury is taxable “compensation” under the Railroad Retirement Tax Act.

586 U.S. 334.name: Rimini Street, Inc. v. Oracle USA, Inc.
586 U.S. 334.source: Supreme Court of the United States
586 U.S. 334.excerpt: A federal district court’s discretion to award “full costs” to a party in copyright litigation pursuant to 17 U. S. C. §505 is limited to the six categories specified in the general costs statute codified at 28 U. S. C. §§1821 and 1920.

586 U.S. 38.name: Escondido v. Emmons
586 U.S. 38.source: Supreme Court of the United States
586 U.S. 38.excerpt: The Ninth Circuit failed to conduct the analysis required by this Court’s precedents in determining whether two Escondido police officers were entitled to qualified immunity.

586 U.S. 392.name: Nielsen v. Preap
586 U.S. 392.source: Supreme Court of the United States
586 U.S. 392.excerpt: The Ninth Circuit’s judgments—that respondents, who are deportable for certain specified crimes, are not subject to 8 U. S. C. §1226(c)(2)’s mandatory-detention requirement because they were not arrested by immigration officials as soon as they were released from jail—are reversed, and the cases are remanded.

586 U.S. 446.name: Air & Liquid Systems Corp. v. DeVries
586 U.S. 446.source: Supreme Court of the United States
586 U.S. 446.excerpt: In the maritime tort context, a product manufacturer has a duty to warn when its product requires incorporation of a part, the manufacturer knows or has reason to know that the integrated product is likely to be dangerous for its intended uses, and the manufacturer has no reason to believe that the product’s users will realize that danger.

586 U.S. 45.name: Shoop v. Hill
586 U.S. 45.source: Supreme Court of the United States
586 U.S. 45.excerpt: Because Hill’s intellectual disability claim must be evaluated based solely on holdings of this Court that were clearly established at the time the state-court decisions were rendered, see 28 U. S. C. §2254(d)(1), the Sixth Circuit’s reliance on Moore v. Texas, 581 U. S. ___—which was handed down much later—was plainly improper.

586 U.S. 485.name: Frank v. Gaos
586 U.S. 485.source: Supreme Court of the United States
586 U.S. 485.excerpt: This class action settlement case is remanded for the courts below to address the plaintiffs’ standing in light of Spokeo, Inc. v. Robins, 578 U. S. ___.

586 U.S. 63.name: Henry Schein, Inc. v. Archer & White Sales, Inc.
586 U.S. 63.source: Supreme Court of the United States
586 U.S. 63.excerpt: The “wholly groundless” exception to the general rule that courts must enforce contracts that delegate threshold arbitrability questions to an arbitrator, not a court, is inconsistent with the Federal Arbitration Act and this Court’s precedent.

586 U.S. 73.name: Stokeling v. United States
586 U.S. 73.source: Supreme Court of the United States
586 U.S. 73.excerpt: The Armed Career Criminal Act’s elements clause encompasses a robbery offense that, like Florida’s law, requires the criminal to overcome the victim’s resistance.

586 U.S. 9.name: Weyerhaeuser Co. v. United States Fish and Wildlife Serv.
586 U.S. 9.source: Supreme Court of the United States
586 U.S. 9.excerpt: An area is eligible for designation as “critical habitat” under the Endangered Species Act of 1973 only if it is habitat for the listed species; and the Secretary of the Interior’s decision not to exclude an area from critical habitat under 16 U. S. C. §1533(b)(2) is subject to judicial review.

587 U.S. 1.name: Republic of Sudan v. Harrison
587 U.S. 1.source: Supreme Court of the United States
587 U.S. 1.excerpt: When civil process is served on a foreign state under the Foreign Sovereign Immunities Act of 1976, 28 U. S. C. §1608(a)(3) requires a mailing to be sent directly to the foreign minister’s office in the foreign state.

587 U.S. 119.name: Bucklew v. Precythe
587 U.S. 119.source: Supreme Court of the United States
587 U.S. 119.excerpt: Baze v. Rees, 553 U. S. 35, and Glossip v. Gross, 576 U. S. ___, govern all Eighth Amendment challenges alleging that a method of execution inflicts unconstitutionally cruel pain; petitioner’s as-applied challenge to Missouri’s single-drug execution protocol—that it would cause him severe pain because of his particular medical condition—fails to satisfy the Baze-Glossip test.

587 U.S. 176.name: Lamps Plus, Inc. v. Varela
587 U.S. 176.source: Supreme Court of the United States
587 U.S. 176.excerpt: Under the Federal Arbitration Act, an ambiguous agreement cannot provide the necessary contractual basis for concluding that the parties agreed to submit to class arbitration.

587 U.S. 218.name: Thacker v. TVA
587 U.S. 218.source: Supreme Court of the United States
587 U.S. 218.excerpt: Title 16 U. S. C. §831c(b), which serves to waive the Tennessee Valley Authority’s sovereign immunity from suit, is not subject to a discretionary function exception of the kind in the Federal Tort Claims Act.

587 U.S. 230.name: Franchise Tax Bd. of Cal. v. Hyatt
587 U.S. 230.source: Supreme Court of the United States
587 U.S. 230.excerpt: Nevada v. Hall, 440 U. S. 410, is overruled; States retain their sovereign immunity from private suits brought in courts of other States.

587 U.S. 262.name: Cochise Consultancy, Inc. v. United States ex rel. Hunt
587 U.S. 262.source: Supreme Court of the United States
587 U.S. 262.excerpt: The limitations period in 31 U. S. C. §3731(b)(2)—which provides that a False Claims Act action must be brought within 3 years after the “the official of the United States charged with responsibility to act in the circumstances” knew or should have known the relevant facts, but not more than 10 years after the violation—applies in a qui tam suit in which the Federal Government has declined to intervene; the relator in a nonintervened suit is not “the official of the United States” whose knowledge triggers §3731(b)(2)’s limitations period.

587 U.S. 28.name: Sturgeon v. Frost
587 U.S. 28.source: Supreme Court of the United States
587 U.S. 28.excerpt: Alaska’s Nation River is not public land; and like all non-public lands and navigable waters within Alaska’s national parks, it is exempt under the Alaska National Interest Lands Conservation Act from the National Park Service’s ordinary regulatory authority.

587 U.S. 299.name: Merck Sharp & Dohme Corp. v. Albrecht
587 U.S. 299.source: Supreme Court of the United States
587 U.S. 299.excerpt: “Clear evidence” that the FDA would not have approved a change to a drug’s label—thus pre-empting a state-law failure-to-warn claim—is evidence showing that the drug manufacturer fully informed the FDA of the justifications for the warning required by state law and that the FDA, in turn, informed the drug manufacturer that the FDA would not approve a change to the drug’s label to include that warning; the question of agency disapproval is primarily one of law for a judge to decide.

587 U.S. 329.name: Herrera v. Wyoming
587 U.S. 329.source: Supreme Court of the United States
587 U.S. 329.excerpt: Wyoming’s statehood did not abrogate the Crow Tribe’s 1868 federal treaty right to hunt on the “unoccupied lands of the United States”; the lands of the Bighorn National Forest did not become categorically “occupied” when the forest was created.

587 U.S. 370.name: Mission Product Holdings, Inc. v. Tempnology, LLC
587 U.S. 370.source: Supreme Court of the United States
587 U.S. 370.excerpt: A bankruptcy debtor’s rejection of an executory contract under 11 U. S. C. §365 has the same effect as a breach of that contract outside bankruptcy; such an act thus cannot rescind rights that the contract previously granted.

587 U.S. 391.name: Nieves v. Bartlett
587 U.S. 391.source: Supreme Court of the United States
587 U.S. 391.excerpt: Because police officers had probable cause to arrest Bartlett, his First Amendment retaliatory arrest claim fails as a matter of law.

587 U.S. 435.name: Home Depot U. S. A., Inc. v. Jackson
587 U.S. 435.source: Supreme Court of the United States
587 U.S. 435.excerpt: Neither the general removal provision, 28 U. S. C. §1441(a), nor the removal provision in the Class Action Fairness Act of 2005, §1453(b), permit a third-party counterclaim defendant to remove a class-action claim from state to federal court.

587 U.S. 471.name: Smith v. Berryhill
587 U.S. 471.source: Supreme Court of the United States
587 U.S. 471.excerpt: A Social Security Administration Appeals Council dismissal on timeliness grounds of a request for review after a claimant has had an administrative law judge hearing on the merits qualifies as a “final decision . . . made after a hearing” for purposes of allowing judicial review under 42 U. S. C. §405(g).

587 U.S. 490.name: Box v. Planned Parenthood of Indiana and Kentucky, Inc.
587 U.S. 490.source: Supreme Court of the United States
587 U.S. 490.excerpt: Indiana’s law relating to the disposition of fetal remains by abortion providers passes rational basis review; certiorari is denied on the question whether the State may bar the knowing provision of sex-, race-, or disability-selective abortions by abortion providers, as only the Seventh Circuit has addressed this kind of law.

587 U.S. 514.name: Mont v. United States
587 U.S. 514.source: Supreme Court of the United States
587 U.S. 514.excerpt: Pretrial detention later credited as time served for a new conviction tolls a supervised-release term under 18 U. S. C. §3624(e), even if the court must make the tolling calculation after learning whether the time will be credited.

587 U.S. 541.name: Fort Bend County v. Davis
587 U.S. 541.source: Supreme Court of the United States
587 U.S. 541.excerpt: The charge-filing precondition to suit set out in Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 is not a jurisdictional requirement.

587 U.S. 554.name: Taggart v. Lorenzen
587 U.S. 554.source: Supreme Court of the United States
587 U.S. 554.excerpt: A creditor may be held in civil contempt for violating a bankruptcy court’s discharge order if there is no fair ground of doubt as to whether the order barred the creditor’s conduct.

587 U.S. 566.name: Azar v. Allina Health Services
587 U.S. 566.source: Supreme Court of the United States
587 U.S. 566.excerpt: Because the Department of Health and Human Services neglected its statutory notice-and-comment obligations when it revealed a new policy that dramatically—and retroactively—reduced Medicare payments to hospitals serving low-income patients, its policy must be vacated.

587 U.S. 601.name: Parker Drilling Management Services, Ltd. v. Newton
587 U.S. 601.source: Supreme Court of the United States
587 U.S. 601.excerpt: Under the Outer Continental Shelf Lands Act, where federal law addresses the relevant issue, state law is not adopted as surrogate federal law on the Outer Continental Shelf.

587 U.S. 645.name: Quarles v. United States
587 U.S. 645.source: Supreme Court of the United States
587 U.S. 645.excerpt: Michigan’s third-degree home-invasion statute substantially corresponds to or is narrower than generic burglary for purposes of qualifying for enhanced sentencing under the Armed Career Criminal Act.

587 U.S. 658.name: Virginia House of Delegates v. Bethune-Hill
587 U.S. 658.source: Supreme Court of the United States
587 U.S. 658.excerpt: The House of Delegates lacks standing to appeal the invalidation of Virginia’s redistricting plan.

587 U.S. 678.name: Gamble v. United States
587 U.S. 678.source: Supreme Court of the United States
587 U.S. 678.excerpt: The dual sovereignty doctrine—under which two offenses are not the “same offence” for double jeopardy purposes if prosecuted by separate sovereigns—is upheld.

587 U.S. 71.name: Lorenzo v. SEC
587 U.S. 71.source: Supreme Court of the United States
587 U.S. 71.excerpt: Dissemination of false or misleading statements with intent to defraud can fall within the scope of SEC Rules 10b–5(a) and (c), as well as the relevant statutory provisions, even if the disseminator cannot be held liable under Rule 10b–5(b).

587 U.S. 761.name: Virginia Uranium, Inc. v. Warren
587 U.S. 761.source: Supreme Court of the United States
587 U.S. 761.excerpt: The Fourth Circuit’s judgment that the Atomic Energy Act does not preempt Virginia’s prohibition on uranium mining in the Commonwealth is affirmed.

587 U.S. 802.name: Manhattan Community Access Corp. v. Halleck
587 U.S. 802.source: Supreme Court of the United States
587 U.S. 802.excerpt: Petitioner, a private nonprofit corporation designated by New York City to operate the public access channels on the Manhattan cable system owned by Time Warner (now Charter), is not a state actor subject to the First Amendment.

587 U.S. 97.name: Biestek v. Berryhill
587 U.S. 97.source: Supreme Court of the United States
587 U.S. 97.excerpt: A vocational expert’s refusal to provide private market-survey data during a Social Security disability benefits hearing upon the applicant’s request does not categorically preclude the testimony from counting as “substantial evidence” in federal court under 42 U. S. C. §405(g).

588 U.S. 1.name: PDR Network, LLC v. Carlton Harris Chiropractic, Inc.
588 U.S. 1.source: Supreme Court of the United States
588 U.S. 1.excerpt: The extent to which a 2006 FCC Order interpreting the term “unsolicited advertisement” binds lower courts may depend on the resolution of two preliminary questions that the Fourth Circuit should address in the first instance: (1) whether the Order is the equivalent of a legislative rule, which has the force and effect of law, or an interpretative rule, which does not; and (2) whether petitioners had a “prior” and “adequate” opportunity to seek judicial review of the Order.

588 U.S. 109.name: McDonough v. Smith
588 U.S. 109.source: Supreme Court of the United States
588 U.S. 109.excerpt: The statute of limitations for McDonough’s 42 U. S. C. §1983 fabricated-evidence claim against his prosecutor began to run when the criminal proceedings against him terminated in his favor—that is, when he was acquitted at the end of his second trial.

588 U.S. 128.name: Gundy v. United States
588 U.S. 128.source: Supreme Court of the United States
588 U.S. 128.excerpt: The Second Circuit’s judgment that 34 U. S. C. §20913(d)—which requires the Attorney General to apply the Sex Offender Registration and Notification Act’s registration requirements as soon as feasible to offenders convicted before the statute’s enactment—is not an unconstitutional delegation of legislative authority is affirmed.

588 U.S. 180.name: Knick v. Township of Scott
588 U.S. 180.source: Supreme Court of the United States
588 U.S. 180.excerpt: A government violates the Takings Clause when it takes property without compensation, and a property owner may bring a Fifth Amendment claim under 42 U. S. C. §1983 at that time; the state-litigation requirement of Williamson County Regional Planning Comm’n v. Hamilton Bank of Johnson City, 473 U. S. 172, is overruled.

588 U.S. 225.name: Rehaif v. United States
588 U.S. 225.source: Supreme Court of the United States
588 U.S. 225.excerpt: In a prosecution under 18 U. S. C. §922(g) and §924(a)(2), the Government must prove both that the defendant knew he possessed a firearm and that he knew he belonged to the relevant category of persons barred from possessing a firearm.

588 U.S. 262.name: North Carolina Dept. of Revenue v. Kimberley Rice Kaestner 1992 Family Trust
588 U.S. 262.source: Supreme Court of the United States
588 U.S. 262.excerpt: The presence of in-state beneficiaries alone does not empower a State to tax trust income that has not been distributed to the beneficiaries where the beneficiaries have no right to demand that income and are uncertain to receive it.

588 U.S. 284.name: Flowers v. Mississippi
588 U.S. 284.source: Supreme Court of the United States
588 U.S. 284.excerpt: The trial court at Flowers’ sixth murder trial committed clear error in concluding that the State’s peremptory strike of a particular black prospective juror was not motivated in substantial part by discriminatory intent.

588 U.S. 29.name: American Legion v. American Humanist Assn.
588 U.S. 29.source: Supreme Court of the United States
588 U.S. 29.excerpt: The Bladensburg Cross does not violate the Establishment Clause.

588 U.S. 358.name: Dutra Group v. Batterton
588 U.S. 358.source: Supreme Court of the United States
588 U.S. 358.excerpt: A plaintiff may not recover punitive damages on a maritime claim of unseaworthiness.

588 U.S. 388.name: Iancu v. Brunetti
588 U.S. 388.source: Supreme Court of the United States
588 U.S. 388.excerpt: The Lanham Act prohibition on the registration of “immoral” or “scandalous” trademarks infringes the First Amendment.

588 U.S. 427.name: Food Marketing Institute v. Argus Leader Media
588 U.S. 427.source: Supreme Court of the United States
588 U.S. 427.excerpt: Where commercial or financial information is both customarily and actually treated as private by its owner and provided to the government under an assurance of privacy, the information is “confidential” within the meaning of 5 U. S. C. §552(b)(4), the Freedom of Information Act’s Exemption 4.

588 U.S. 445.name: United States v. Davis
588 U.S. 445.source: Supreme Court of the United States
588 U.S. 445.excerpt: Title 18 U. S. C. §924(c)(3)(B), which provides enhanced penalties for using a firearm during a “crime of violence,” is unconstitutionally vague.

588 U.S. 504.name: Tennessee Wine and Spirits Retailers Assn. v. Thomas
588 U.S. 504.source: Supreme Court of the United States
588 U.S. 504.excerpt: Tennessee’s 2-year durational-residency requirement applicable to retail liquor store license applicants violates the Commerce Clause and is not saved by the Twenty-first Amendment.

588 U.S. 558.name: Kisor v. Wilkie
588 U.S. 558.source: Supreme Court of the United States
588 U.S. 558.excerpt: Auer v. Robbins, 519 U. S. 452, and Bowles v. Seminole Rock & Sand Co., 325 U. S. 410—under which deference is given to an agency’s reasonable reading of its own genuinely ambiguous regulations—are not overruled.

588 U.S. 634.name: United States v. Haymond
588 U.S. 634.source: Supreme Court of the United States
588 U.S. 634.excerpt: The Tenth Circuit’s judgment—that 18 U. S. C. §3583(k)’s last two sentences are unconstitutional and unenforceable—is vacated, and the case is remanded.

588 U.S. 684.name: Rucho v. Common Cause
588 U.S. 684.source: Supreme Court of the United States
588 U.S. 684.excerpt: Partisan gerrymandering claims present political questions beyond the reach of the federal courts.

588 U.S. 752.name: Department of Commerce v. New York
588 U.S. 752.source: Supreme Court of the United States
588 U.S. 752.excerpt: The Secretary did not violate the Enumeration Clause or the Census Act in deciding to reinstate a citizenship question on the 2020 census questionnaire, but the District Court was warranted in remanding the case back to the agency where the evidence tells a story that does not match the Secretary’s explanation for his decision.

588 U.S. 840.name: Mitchell v. Wisconsin
588 U.S. 840.source: Supreme Court of the United States
588 U.S. 840.excerpt: The Wisconsin Supreme Court’s judgment—affirming the drunk-driving convictions of petitioner Mitchell, who was administered a warrantless blood test while he was unconscious—is vacated, and the case is remanded.

589 U.S. 1.name: Thompson v. Hebdon
589 U.S. 1.source: Supreme Court of the United States
589 U.S. 1.excerpt: The judgment is vacated, and the case is remanded for the Ninth Circuit to revisit whether Alaska’s political contribution limits are consistent with this Court’s First Amendment precedents.

589 U.S. 132.name: Rodriguez v. FDIC
589 U.S. 132.source: Supreme Court of the United States
589 U.S. 132.excerpt: The rule of In re Bob Richards Chrysler-Plymouth Corp., 473 F. 2d 262—which specifies how federal tax refund proceeds should be allocated among members of an affiliated group of corporations that file a consolidated return—is not a legitimate exercise of federal common lawmaking.

589 U.S. 139.name: McKinney v. Arizona
589 U.S. 139.source: Supreme Court of the United States
589 U.S. 139.excerpt: When a capital sentencing error under Eddings v. Oklahoma, 455 U. S. 104, is found on collateral review, a state appellate court may conduct the reweighing of aggravating and mitigating evidence, as permitted by Clemons v. Mississippi, 494 U. S. 738, on collateral review.

589 U.S. 154.name: Shular v. United States
589 U.S. 154.source: Supreme Court of the United States
589 U.S. 154.excerpt: For purposes of the Armed Career Criminal Act’s sentence enhancement for a defendant convicted of being a felon in possession of a firearm who has at least three convictions for “serious drug offense[s],” 18 U. S. C. §924(e)(1), the “serious drug offense” definition requires only that a state offense involve the conduct specified in the statute; it does not require that the state offense match certain generic offenses.

589 U.S. 169.name: Holguin-Hernandez v. United States
589 U.S. 169.source: Supreme Court of the United States
589 U.S. 169.excerpt: Petitioner’s district-court argument for a specific sentence (nothing or less than 12 months) preserved, for purposes of Fed. Rule Crim. Proc. 51(b), his claim on appeal that the sentence imposed was unreasonably long.

589 U.S. 178.name: Intel Corp. Investment Policy Comm. v. Sulyma
589 U.S. 178.source: Supreme Court of the United States
589 U.S. 178.excerpt: Under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974 requirement that plaintiffs with “actual knowledge” of an alleged fiduciary breach must file suit within three years of gaining that knowledge, 29 U. S. C. §1113(2), a plaintiff does not necessarily have “actual knowledge” of the information contained in disclosures that he receives but does not read or cannot recall reading.

589 U.S. 191.name: Kansas v. Garcia
589 U.S. 191.source: Supreme Court of the United States
589 U.S. 191.excerpt: The Kansas statutes under which respondents, three unauthorized aliens, were convicted—for fraudulently using another person’s Social Security number on state and federal tax-withholding forms submitted to their employers—are not expressly preempted by the Immigration Reform and Control Act of 1986; and respondents’ argument that those laws are preempted by implication is rejected.

589 U.S. 221.name: Guerrero-Lasprilla v. Barr
589 U.S. 221.source: Supreme Court of the United States
589 U.S. 221.excerpt: Because the phrase “questions of law” in the Immigration and Nationality Act’s Limited Review Provision, 8 U. S. C. §1252(a)(2)(D), includes the application of a legal standard to undisputed or established facts, the Fifth Circuit erred in holding that it had no jurisdiction to consider petitioners’ “factual” due diligence claims for equitable tolling purposes.

589 U.S. 23.name: Peter v. NantKwest, Inc.
589 U.S. 23.source: Supreme Court of the United States
589 U.S. 23.excerpt: The Patent and Trademark Office cannot recover the salaries of its legal personnel as “expenses” in civil actions brought by patent applicants pursuant to 35 U. S. C. §145.

589 U.S. 248.name: Allen v. Cooper
589 U.S. 248.source: Supreme Court of the United States
589 U.S. 248.excerpt: Congress lacked authority to abrogate the States’ sovereign immunity from copyright infringement suits in the Copyright Remedy Clarification Act of 1990.

589 U.S. 271.name: Kahler v. Kansas
589 U.S. 271.source: Supreme Court of the United States
589 U.S. 271.excerpt: Due process does not require Kansas to adopt an insanity test that turns on a defendant’s ability to recognize that his crime was morally wrong.

589 U.S. 327.name: Comcast Corp. v. National Assn. of African-American Owned Media
589 U.S. 327.source: Supreme Court of the United States
589 U.S. 327.excerpt: A plaintiff who sues for racial discrimination in contracting under 42 U. S. C. §1981 bears the burden of showing that race was a but-for cause of the plaintiff’s injury, and that burden remains constant over the life of the lawsuit.

589 U.S. 35.name: Ritzen Group, Inc. v. Jackson Masonry, LLC
589 U.S. 35.source: Supreme Court of the United States
589 U.S. 35.excerpt: A bankruptcy court’s order unreservedly denying relief from the automatic stay of creditor debt-collection efforts outside the bankruptcy forum, see 11 U. S. C. §362(a), is final and immediately appealable under 28 U. S. C. §158(a).

589 U.S. 376.name: Kansas v. Glover
589 U.S. 376.source: Supreme Court of the United States
589 U.S. 376.excerpt: When a police officer lacks information negating an inference that a person driving is the vehicle’s owner, an investigative traffic stop made after running the vehicle’s license plate and learning that the registered owner’s driver’s license has been revoked is reasonable under the Fourth Amendment.

589 U.S. 399.name: Babb v. Wilkie
589 U.S. 399.source: Supreme Court of the United States
589 U.S. 399.excerpt: The plain meaning of 29 U. S. C. §633a(a), the federal-sector provision of the Age Discrimination in Employment Act of 1967, demands that personnel actions be untainted by any consideration of age, but but-for causation is important in determining the appropriate remedy that may be obtained.

589 U.S. 423.name: Republican National Committee v. Democratic National Committee
589 U.S. 423.source: Supreme Court of the United States
589 U.S. 423.excerpt: The District Court’s order granting a preliminary injunction is stayed to the extent it requires Wisconsin to count absentee ballots postmarked after April 7, 2020, the date of the State’s election.

589 U.S. 49.name: Retirement Plans Comm. of IBM v. Jander
589 U.S. 49.source: Supreme Court of the United States
589 U.S. 49.excerpt: The judgment is vacated, and the case is remanded to give the Second Circuit the opportunity to decide whether to entertain the parties’ arguments on ERISA’s duty of prudence.

589 U.S. 57.name: Roman Catholic Archdiocese of San Juan v. Acevedo Feliciano
589 U.S. 57.source: Supreme Court of the United States
589 U.S. 57.excerpt: A Puerto Rico trial court had no jurisdiction to issue payment and seizure orders after a pension benefits proceeding was removed to Federal District Court but before the proceeding was remanded back to the Puerto Rico court; thus the orders are void.

589 U.S. 68.name: Monasky v. Taglieri
589 U.S. 68.source: Supreme Court of the United States
589 U.S. 68.excerpt: Under the Hague Convention on the Civil Aspects of International Child Abduction, a child’s “habitual residence” depends on the totality of the circumstances specific to the case, not on categorical requirements such as an actual agreement between the parties.

589 U.S. 8.name: Rotkiske v. Klemm
589 U.S. 8.source: Supreme Court of the United States
589 U.S. 8.excerpt: Absent the application of an equitable doctrine, the Federal Debt Collection Practices Act’s statute of limitations for bringing a private civil action against debt collectors who engage in certain prohibited practices, 15 U. S. C. §1692k(d), begins to run when the alleged violation occurs, not when it is discovered.

589 U.S. 93.name: Hernández v. Mesa
589 U.S. 93.source: Supreme Court of the United States
589 U.S. 93.excerpt: A cross-border shooting by a United States Border Patrol agent does not give rise to a damages claim pursuant to Bivens v. Six Unknown Fed. Narcotics Agents, 403 U. S. 388.

59 U.S. 272.name: Murray's Lessee et al. v. Hoboken Land and Improvement Co.
59 U.S. 272.source: Library of Congress, United States Reports

59 U.S. 421.name: State of Pennsylvania v. Wheeling and Belmont Bridge Co.
59 U.S. 421.source: Library of Congress, United States Reports

59 U.S. 460.name: State of Pennsylvania v. Wheeling and Belmont Bridge Co.
59 U.S. 460.source: Library of Congress, United States Reports

590 U.S. 1.name: Atlantic Richfield Co. v. Christian
590 U.S. 1.source: Supreme Court of the United States
590 U.S. 1.excerpt: The Montana Supreme Court erred by holding that respondent landowners were not potentially responsible parties under the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act and thus did not need the Environmental Protection Agency’s approval to take remedial action.

590 U.S. 165.name: County of Maui v. Hawaii Wildlife Fund
590 U.S. 165.source: Supreme Court of the United States
590 U.S. 165.excerpt: The Clean Water Act, which forbids “any addition” of any pollutant from “any point source” to “navigable waters” without the appropriate Environmental Protection Agency permit, 33 U. S. C. §§1311(a), 1362(12)(A), requires a permit when there is a direct discharge from a point source into navigable waters or when there is the functional equivalent of a direct discharge.

590 U.S. 212.name: Romag Fasteners, Inc. v. Fossil Group, Inc.
590 U.S. 212.source: Supreme Court of the United States
590 U.S. 212.excerpt: A plaintiff in a trademark infringement suit is not required to show that a defendant willfully infringed the plaintiff’s trademark as a precondition to an award of profits.

590 U.S. 222.name: Barton v. Barr
590 U.S. 222.source: Supreme Court of the United States
590 U.S. 222.excerpt: In determining eligibility for cancellation of removal of a lawful permanent resident who commits a serious crime, an offense listed in 8 U. S. C. §1182(a)(2) committed during the initial seven years of residence need not be one of the offenses of removal.

590 U.S. 255.name: Georgia v. Public Resource.Org, Inc.
590 U.S. 255.source: Supreme Court of the United States
590 U.S. 255.excerpt: Under the government edicts doctrine, the annotations beneath the statutory provisions in the Official Code of Georgia Annotated are ineligible for copyright protection.

590 U.S. 296.name: Maine Community Health Options v. United States
590 U.S. 296.source: Supreme Court of the United States
590 U.S. 296.excerpt: The Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act’s now expired “Risk Corridors” statute—which set a formula for calculating payments to healthcare insurers for unexpectedly unprofitable plans during the first three years of online insurance marketplaces—created a Government obligation to pay insurers the full amount of their computed losses; and petitioners properly relied on the Tucker Act to sue for damages in the Court of Federal Claims.

590 U.S. 336.name: New York State Rifle & Pistol Assn., Inc. v. City of New York
590 U.S. 336.source: Supreme Court of the United States
590 U.S. 336.excerpt: Petitioners’ claim for declaratory and injunctive relief with respect to the City’s old rule on transporting firearms is moot, and any claim for damages with respect to that rule may be addressed in the first instance by the Court of Appeals and the District Court on remand.

590 U.S. 371.name: United States v. Sineneng-Smith
590 U.S. 371.source: Supreme Court of the United States
590 U.S. 371.excerpt: The Ninth Circuit panel’s drastic departure from the principle of party presentation constituted an abuse of discretion where the court reached out to decide a question never raised by respondent, namely, whether 8 U. S. C. §1324(a)(1)(A)(iv) is unconstitutionally overbroad.

590 U.S. 391.name: Kelly v. United States
590 U.S. 391.source: Supreme Court of the United States
590 U.S. 391.excerpt: Because the scheme to reduce the number of George Washington Bridge toll lanes dedicated to Fort Lee, New Jersey, morning commuters as political retribution against Fort Lee’s mayor did not aim to obtain money or property from the federal Port Authority, Baroni and Kelly could not have violated the federal-program fraud or wire fraud laws.

590 U.S. 405.name: Lucky Brand Dungarees, Inc. v. Marcel Fashions Group, Inc.
590 U.S. 405.source: Supreme Court of the United States
590 U.S. 405.excerpt: Because the trademark action at issue challenged different conduct—and raised different claims—from an earlier action between the parties, Marcel cannot preclude Lucky Brand from raising new defenses, including a defense that Lucky Brand failed to press fully in the earlier suit.

590 U.S. 418.name: Opati v. Republic of Sudan
590 U.S. 418.source: Supreme Court of the United States
590 U.S. 418.excerpt: Plaintiffs in a suit against a foreign state for personal injury or death caused by acts of terrorism under 28 U. S. C. §1605A(c) may seek punitive damages for preenactment conduct.

590 U.S. 432.name: GE Energy Power Conversion France SAS v. Outokumpu Stainless USA, LLC
590 U.S. 432.source: Supreme Court of the United States
590 U.S. 432.excerpt: The Convention on the Recognition and Enforcement of Foreign Arbitral Awards does not conflict with domestic equitable estoppel doctrines that permit the enforcement of arbitration agreements by nonsignatories to those agreements.

590 U.S. 448.name: Financial Oversight and Management Bd. for Puerto Rico v. Aurelius Investment, LLC
590 U.S. 448.source: Supreme Court of the United States
590 U.S. 448.excerpt: The Appointments Clause does not restrict the appointment or selection of members of Puerto Rico’s Financial Oversight and Management Board, who are appointed by the President without the Senate’s advice and consent.

590 U.S. 45.name: Thryv, Inc. v. Click-To-Call Technologies, LP
590 U.S. 45.source: Supreme Court of the United States
590 U.S. 45.excerpt: Title 35 U. S. C. §314(d) precludes judicial review of a Patent Trial and Appeal Board’s decision to institute inter partes review upon finding that §315(b)’s time bar did not apply.

590 U.S. 504.name: Banister v. Davis
590 U.S. 504.source: Supreme Court of the United States
590 U.S. 504.excerpt: Because a Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 59(e) motion to alter or amend a habeas court’s judgment is not a second or successive habeas petition under 28 U. S. C. §2244(b), Banister’s appeal was timely.

590 U.S. 538.name: Thole v. U. S. Bank N. A.
590 U.S. 538.source: Supreme Court of the United States
590 U.S. 538.excerpt: Because petitioners, whose defined-benefit retirement plan guarantees them a fixed payment each month regardless of the plan’s value or its fiduciaries’ investment decisions, have no concrete stake in this Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974 lawsuit against the fiduciaries, they lack Article III standing.

590 U.S. 573.name: Nasrallah v. Barr
590 U.S. 573.source: Supreme Court of the United States
590 U.S. 573.excerpt: Title 8 U. S. C. §§1252(a)(2)(C) and (D) do not preclude judicial review of a removable noncitizen’s factual challenges to an order denying relief under the international Convention Against Torture, which protects noncitizens from removal to a country where they would likely face torture.

590 U.S. 595.name: Lomax v. Ortiz-Marquez
590 U.S. 595.source: Supreme Court of the United States
590 U.S. 595.excerpt: A Prison Litigation Reform Act of 1995 provision that generally prevents a prisoner from bringing suit in forma pauperis if he has had three or more prior suits “dismissed on the ground[ ] that [they] . . . fail[ed] to state a claim upon which relief may be granted,” 28 U. S. C. §1915(g), refers to any dismissal for failure to state a claim, whether with prejudice or without.

590 U.S. 604.name: United States Forest Service v. Cowpasture River Preservation Assn.
590 U.S. 604.source: Supreme Court of the United States
590 U.S. 604.excerpt: Because the Department of the Interior’s decision to assign responsibility over the Appalachian Trail to the National Park Service did not transform the land over which the Trail passes into land within the National Park System, the Forest Service had authority under the Mineral Leasing Act to grant a natural-gas pipeline right-of-way through lands in the George Washington National Forest traversed by the Appalachian Trail.

590 U.S. 644.name: Bostock v. Clayton County
590 U.S. 644.source: Supreme Court of the United States
590 U.S. 644.excerpt: An employer who fires an individual merely for being gay or transgender violates Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964.

590 U.S. 806.name: Andrus v. Texas
590 U.S. 806.source: Supreme Court of the United States
590 U.S. 806.excerpt: Because there is a significant question whether the court below properly considered whether counsel’s clearly deficient performance prejudiced Andrus, the judgment of the Texas Court of Criminal Appeals is vacated and the case is remanded for the court to address the prejudice question.

590 U.S. 83.name: Ramos v. Louisiana
590 U.S. 83.source: Supreme Court of the United States
590 U.S. 83.excerpt: The Louisiana Court of Appeal’s holding that nonunanimous jury verdicts are constitutional is reversed.

591 U.S. 1.name: Department of Homeland Security v. Regents of Univ. of Cal.
591 U.S. 1.source: Supreme Court of the United States
591 U.S. 1.excerpt: The Department of Homeland Security’s decision to rescind the Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals program was arbitrary and capricious under the Administrative Procedure Act.

591 U.S. 103.name: Department of Homeland Security v. Thuraissigiam
591 U.S. 103.source: Supreme Court of the United States
591 U.S. 103.excerpt: As applied here, 8 U. S. C. §1252(e)(2)—which limits the habeas review obtainable by an alien detained for expedited removal—does not violate the Suspension or Due Process Clauses.

591 U.S. 197.name: Seila Law LLC v. Consumer Financial Protection Bureau
591 U.S. 197.source: Supreme Court of the United States
591 U.S. 197.excerpt: The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau’s leadership by a single Director removable only for inefficiency, neglect, or malfeasance violates the separation of powers.

591 U.S. 299.name: June Medical Services L. L. C. v. Russo
591 U.S. 299.source: Supreme Court of the United States
591 U.S. 299.excerpt: The Fifth Circuit’s judgment, upholding a Louisiana law that requires abortion providers to hold admitting privileges at local hospitals, is reversed.

591 U.S. 430.name: Agency for Int’l Development v. Alliance for Open Society
591 U.S. 430.source: Supreme Court of the United States
591 U.S. 430.excerpt: Because the foreign affiliates of American nongovernmental organizations possess no First Amendment rights, the United States Leadership Against HIV/AIDS, Tuberculosis, and Malaria Act’s limitation on funding organizations with “a policy explicitly opposing prostitution and sex trafficking,” 22 U. S. C. §7631(f), is not unconstitutional as applied to them.

591 U.S. 464.name: Espinoza v. Montana Dept. of Revenue
591 U.S. 464.source: Supreme Court of the United States
591 U.S. 464.excerpt: The application of the Montana Constitution’s “no-aid” provision to a state program providing tuition assistance to parents who send their children to private schools discriminated against religious schools and the families whose children attend or hope to attend them in violation of the Federal Constitution’s Free Exercise Clause.

591 U.S. 549.name: Patent and Trademark Office v. Booking.com B. V.
591 U.S. 549.source: Supreme Court of the United States
591 U.S. 549.excerpt: A term styled “generic.com” is a generic name for a class of goods or services—and thus ineligible for federal trademark protection—only if the term has that meaning to consumers.

591 U.S. 578.name: Chiafalo v. Washington
591 U.S. 578.source: Supreme Court of the United States
591 U.S. 578.excerpt: A State may enforce an elector’s pledge to support his party’s nominee—and the state voters’ choice—for President.

591 U.S. 610.name: Barr v. American Assn. of Political Consultants, Inc.
591 U.S. 610.source: Supreme Court of the United States
591 U.S. 610.excerpt: The Fourth Circuit’s judgment—that the robocall restriction’s government-debt exception in 47 U. S. C. §227(b)(1)(A)(iii) violates the First Amendment but is severable from the remainder of the statute—is affirmed.

591 U.S. 657.name: Little Sisters of the Poor Saints Peter and Paul Home v. Pennsylvania
591 U.S. 657.source: Supreme Court of the United States
591 U.S. 657.excerpt: The Departments of Health and Human Services, Labor, and the Treasury had authority under the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act of 2010 to promulgate rules exempting employers with religious or moral objections from providing contraceptive coverage to their employees; and those rules satisfy the Administrative Procedure Act’s notice requirements.

591 U.S. 71.name: Liu v. SEC
591 U.S. 71.source: Supreme Court of the United States
591 U.S. 71.excerpt: In a Securities and Exchange Commission enforcement action, a disgorgement award that does not exceed a wrongdoer’s net profits and is awarded for victims is equitable relief permissible under 15 U. S. C. §78u(d)(5).

591 U.S. 732.name: Our Lady of Guadalupe School v. Morrissey-Berru
591 U.S. 732.source: Supreme Court of the United States
591 U.S. 732.excerpt: The First Amendment’s Religion Clauses foreclose the adjudication of the employment-discrimination claims of Catholic school teachers Morrissey-Berru and Biel.

591 U.S. 786.name: Trump v. Vance
591 U.S. 786.source: Supreme Court of the United States
591 U.S. 786.excerpt: Article II and the Supremacy Clause do not categorically preclude, or require a heightened standard for, the issuance of a state criminal subpoena to a sitting President.

591 U.S. 848.name: Trump v. Mazars USA, LLP
591 U.S. 848.source: Supreme Court of the United States
591 U.S. 848.excerpt: The courts below did not take adequate account of the significant separation of powers concerns implicated by congressional subpoenas for the President’s information.

591 U.S. 894.name: McGirt v. Oklahoma
591 U.S. 894.source: Supreme Court of the United States
591 U.S. 894.excerpt: Land in Northeastern Oklahoma reserved for the Creek Nation since the 19th century remains “Indian country” for purposes of the Major Crimes Act, which places certain crimes under federal jurisdiction if they were committed by “[a]ny Indian” within “the Indian country.” 18 U. S. C. §1153(a).

591 U.S. 979.name: Barr v. Lee
591 U.S. 979.source: Supreme Court of the United States
591 U.S. 979.excerpt: The District Court’s order preliminarily enjoining the executions of four federal prisoners is vacated.

592 U.S. 1.name: Mckesson v. Doe
592 U.S. 1.source: Supreme Court of the United States
592 U.S. 1.excerpt: Under the unusual circumstances of this case, the Fifth Circuit should not have ventured into such an uncertain area of state tort law without first using state certification procedures to seek guidance from the Louisiana Supreme Court.

592 U.S. 111.name: Shinn v. Kayer
592 U.S. 111.source: Supreme Court of the United States
592 U.S. 111.excerpt: Under the deferential standard of the Antiterrorism and Effective Death Penalty Act of 1996, the Ninth Circuit exceeded its authority in rejecting the state court’s determination that Kayer failed to show prejudice in his ineffective-assistance-of-counsel claim.

592 U.S. 125.name: Trump v. New York
592 U.S. 125.source: Supreme Court of the United States
592 U.S. 125.excerpt: Because plaintiffs have not shown standing and because the claims presented are not ripe for adjudication, the District Court’s judgment is vacated, and the case is remanded with instructions to dismiss for lack of jurisdiction.

592 U.S. 14.name: Roman Catholic Diocese of Brooklyn v. Cuomo
592 U.S. 14.source: Supreme Court of the United States
592 U.S. 14.excerpt: Respondent is enjoined from enforcing Executive Order 202.68’s 10- and 25-person occupancy limits on Applicant pending disposition of the appeal in the United States Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit and disposition of the petition for a writ of certiorari, if such writ is timely sought.

592 U.S. 154.name: Chicago v. Fulton
592 U.S. 154.source: Supreme Court of the United States
592 U.S. 154.excerpt: The mere retention of estate property after the filing of a bankruptcy petition does not violate 11 U. S. C. §362(a)(3), which operates as a “stay” of “any act” to “exercise control” over the property of the estate.

592 U.S. 169.name: Federal Republic of Germany v. Philipp
592 U.S. 169.source: Supreme Court of the United States
592 U.S. 169.excerpt: The Foreign Sovereign Immunities Act’s expropriation exception, 28 U. S. C. §1605(a)(3), incorporates the domestic takings rule, which recognizes that a foreign sovereign’s taking of its own nationals’ property is not a violation of international law.

592 U.S. 188.name: Salinas v. Railroad Retirement Bd.
592 U.S. 188.source: Supreme Court of the United States
592 U.S. 188.excerpt: The U. S. Railroad Retirement Board’s denial of a request to reopen a prior benefits determination under the Railroad Retirement Act of 1974 and the Railroad Unemployment Insurance Act is subject to judicial review.

592 U.S. 209.name: Brownback v. King
592 U.S. 209.source: Supreme Court of the United States
592 U.S. 209.excerpt: The District Court’s order dismissing King’s Federal Tort Claims Act claims was a judgment on the merits that can trigger the Act’s judgment bar to block his Bivens claims. See 28 U. S. C. §2676; Bivens v. Six Unknown Fed. Narcotics Agents, 403 U. S. 388.

592 U.S. 224.name: Pereida v. Wilkinson
592 U.S. 224.source: Supreme Court of the United States
592 U.S. 224.excerpt: A nonpermanent resident seeking to cancel a lawful removal order fails to carry his burden of showing that he has not been convicted of a disqualifying offense when the statutory conviction on his record is ambiguous regarding whether a disqualifying offense formed the basis of his conviction.

592 U.S. 261.name: United States Fish and Wildlife Serv. v. Sierra Club, Inc.
592 U.S. 261.source: Supreme Court of the United States
592 U.S. 261.excerpt: The deliberative process privilege protects from disclosure under FOIA in-house draft biological opinions that are both predecisional and deliberative, even if the drafts reflect the agencies’ last views about a proposal.

592 U.S. 279.name: Uzuegbunam v. Preczewski
592 U.S. 279.source: Supreme Court of the United States
592 U.S. 279.excerpt: A request for nominal damages satisfies the redressability element necessary for Article III standing where a plaintiff’s claim is based on a completed violation of a legal right.

592 U.S. 306.name: Torres v. Madrid
592 U.S. 306.source: Supreme Court of the United States
592 U.S. 306.excerpt: Application of physical force to the body of a person with intent to restrain is a seizure even if the person does not submit and is not subdued.

592 U.S. 351.name: Ford Motor Co. v. Montana Eighth Judicial Dist.
592 U.S. 351.source: Supreme Court of the United States
592 U.S. 351.excerpt: The connection between plaintiffs’ product-liability claims arising from car accidents occurring in each plaintiff’s State of residence and Ford’s activities in those States is sufficient to support specific jurisdiction in the respective State courts even though the automobiles involved in the accidents were manufactured and sold elsewhere.

592 U.S. 385.name: Mays v. Hines
592 U.S. 385.source: Supreme Court of the United States
592 U.S. 385.excerpt: The Sixth Circuit erred in revisiting on federal habeas review the decision of a Tennessee court supported by ample evidence that did not exceed the possibility of fairminded disagreement.

592 U.S. 395.name: Facebook, Inc. v. Duguid
592 U.S. 395.source: Supreme Court of the United States
592 U.S. 395.excerpt: To qualify as an “automatic telephone dialing system” under the Telephone Consumer Protection Act of 1991, a device must have the capacity either to store, or to produce, a telephone number using a random or sequential number generator.

592 U.S. 414.name: FCC v. Prometheus Radio Project
592 U.S. 414.source: Supreme Court of the United States
592 U.S. 414.excerpt: The Federal Communications Commission’s 2017 decision to repeal or modify three of its media ownership rules was not arbitrary or capricious for purposes of the Administrative Procedure Act.

592 U.S. 43.name: Tanzin v. Tanvir
592 U.S. 43.source: Supreme Court of the United States
592 U.S. 43.excerpt: The Religious Freedom Restoration Act of 1993’s express remedies provision, see 42 U. S. C. §2000bb–1(c), permits litigants, when appropriate, to obtain money damages against federal officials in their individual capacities.

592 U.S. 433.name: Florida v. Georgia
592 U.S. 433.source: Supreme Court of the United States
592 U.S. 433.excerpt: Florida fails to establish that Georgia’s overconsumption of interstate waters was either a substantial factor contributing to, or the sole cause of, Florida’s injuries.

592 U.S. 53.name: Carney v. Adams
592 U.S. 53.source: Supreme Court of the United States
592 U.S. 53.excerpt: Because plaintiff Adams has not shown that he was “able and ready” to apply for a judicial vacancy in the imminent future, Gratz v. Bollinger, 539 U. S. 244, 262, he has failed to demonstrate Article III standing to challenge the Delaware Constitution’s political balance requirement for appointments to the State’s major courts.

592 U.S. 7.name: Taylor v. Riojas
592 U.S. 7.source: Supreme Court of the United States
592 U.S. 7.excerpt: Because any reasonable correctional officer should have realized that inmate Taylor’s conditions of confinement offended the Eighth Amendment, the Fifth Circuit erred in granting the officers qualified immunity.

592 U.S. 80.name: Rutledge v. Pharmaceutical Care Management Assn.
592 U.S. 80.source: Supreme Court of the United States
592 U.S. 80.excerpt: Arkansas’ Act 900—which effectively requires pharmacy benefit managers to reimburse Arkansas pharmacies for the cost of drugs covered by prescription-drug plans at a price equal to or higher than the pharmacy’s wholesale cost—is not pre-empted by the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974.

593 U.S. 1.name: Google LLC v. Oracle America, Inc.
593 U.S. 1.source: Supreme Court of the United States
593 U.S. 1.excerpt: Google’s limited copying of the Java SE Application Programming Interface allowed programmers to put their accrued talents to work in a transformative program and constituted a fair use of that material under copyright law.

593 U.S. 155.name: Niz-Chavez v. Garland
593 U.S. 155.source: Supreme Court of the United States
593 U.S. 155.excerpt: A notice to appear sufficient to trigger the Illegal Immigration Reform and Immigrant Responsibility Act of 1996’s stop-time rule is a single document containing all the information about an individual’s removal hearing specified in 8 U. S. C. §1229(a)(1).

593 U.S. 194.name: Caniglia v. Strom
593 U.S. 194.source: Supreme Court of the United States
593 U.S. 194.excerpt: Neither the holding nor logic of Cady v. Dombrowski, 413 U. S. 433, justifies the removal of Caniglia’s firearms from his home by police officers under a “community caretaking exception” to the Fourth Amendment’s warrant requirement.

593 U.S. 209.name: CIC Servs., LLC v. IRS
593 U.S. 209.source: Supreme Court of the United States
593 U.S. 209.excerpt: A suit to enjoin IRS Notice 2016–66 does not trigger the Anti-Injunction Act even though a violation of the Notice may result in a tax penalty.

593 U.S. 230.name: BP p.l.c. v. Mayor and City Council of Baltimore
593 U.S. 230.source: Supreme Court of the United States
593 U.S. 230.excerpt: Where defendant energy companies premised 28 U. S. C. §1447(d) removal in part on the federal officer removal statute, §1442, the Fourth Circuit erred in holding that it lacked jurisdiction to consider all grounds for removal rejected by the District Court.

593 U.S. 255.name: Edwards v. Vannoy
593 U.S. 255.source: Supreme Court of the United States
593 U.S. 255.excerpt: The jury-unanimity rule announced in Ramos v. Louisiana, 590 U. S. ___, does not apply retroactively on federal collateral review.

593 U.S. 310.name: Guam v. United States
593 U.S. 310.source: Supreme Court of the United States
593 U.S. 310.excerpt: A settlement of environmental liabilities must resolve a specific liability under the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act of 1980 to give rise to a contribution action under that Act.

593 U.S. 321.name: United States v. Palomar-Santiago
593 U.S. 321.source: Supreme Court of the United States
593 U.S. 321.excerpt: Each of 8 U. S. C. §1326(d)’s statutory requirements for bringing a collateral attack on a prior deportation order is mandatory.

593 U.S. 345.name: United States v. Cooley
593 U.S. 345.source: Supreme Court of the United States
593 U.S. 345.excerpt: A tribal police officer has authority to detain temporarily and to search a non-Indian traveling on a public right-of-way running through a reservation for potential violations of state or federal law.

593 U.S. 357.name: Garland v. Ming Dai
593 U.S. 357.source: Supreme Court of the United States
593 U.S. 357.excerpt: The Ninth Circuit’s rule in immigration disputes—that in the absence of an explicit adverse credibility determination by an immigration judge or the Board of Immigration Appeals, a reviewing court must treat a petitioning noncitizen’s testimony as credible and true—cannot be reconciled with the terms of the Immigration and Nationality Act.

593 U.S. 374.name: Van Buren v. United States
593 U.S. 374.source: Supreme Court of the United States
593 U.S. 374.excerpt: An individual “exceeds authorized access” under the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act of 1986, 18 U. S. C. §1030(a)(2), when he accesses a computer with authorization but then obtains information located in particular areas of the computer—such as files, folders, or databases—that are off-limits to him.

593 U.S. 409.name: Sanchez v. Mayorkas
593 U.S. 409.source: Supreme Court of the United States
593 U.S. 409.excerpt: An individual who entered the United States unlawfully is not eligible to become a lawful permanent resident under 8 U.S.C. §1255 even if the United States has granted the individual temporary protected status.

593 U.S. 420.name: Borden v. United States
593 U.S. 420.source: Supreme Court of the United States
593 U.S. 420.excerpt: The decision of the Sixth Circuit—holding that an offense with a mental state of recklessness may qualify as a “violent felony” under the Armed Career Criminal Act’s elements clause, 18 U. S. C. §924(e)(2)(B)(i)—is reversed, and the case is remanded.

593 U.S. 486.name: Terry v. United States
593 U.S. 486.source: Supreme Court of the United States
593 U.S. 486.excerpt: A sentence reduction under the First Step Act is available only if an offender’s prior conviction of a crack cocaine offense triggered a mandatory minimum sentence.

593 U.S. 503.name: Greer v. United States
593 U.S. 503.source: Supreme Court of the United States
593 U.S. 503.excerpt: In felon-in-possession cases under 18 U. S. C. §922(g)(1), an error under Rehaif v. United States, 588 U. S. ___, is not a basis for plain-error relief unless the defendant first makes a sufficient argument or representation on appeal that he would have presented evidence at trial that he did not in fact know he was a felon.

593 U.S. 522.name: Fulton v. Philadelphia
593 U.S. 522.source: Supreme Court of the United States
593 U.S. 522.excerpt: Philadelphia’s refusal to contract with Catholic Social Services for the provision of foster care services unless CSS agrees to certify same-sex couples as foster parents violates the Free Exercise Clause of the First Amendment.

593 U.S. 61.name: Tandon v. Newsom
593 U.S. 61.source: Supreme Court of the United States
593 U.S. 61.excerpt: California is enjoined from enforcing that State’s COVID–19 restrictions on private gatherings as applied to applicants’ at-home religious exercise pending disposition of the appeal in the United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit and disposition of the petition for a writ of certiorari, if any.

593 U.S. 628.name: Nestlé USA, Inc. v. Doe
593 U.S. 628.source: Supreme Court of the United States
593 U.S. 628.excerpt: To plead facts sufficient to support a domestic application of the Alien Tort Statute, 28 U. S. C. §1350, plaintiffs must allege more domestic conduct than general corporate activity; the Ninth Circuit’s contrary holding is reversed, and the case is remanded.

593 U.S. 659.name: California v. Texas
593 U.S. 659.source: Supreme Court of the United States
593 U.S. 659.excerpt: Plaintiffs lack standing to challenge the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act’s minimum essential coverage provision.

593 U.S. 67.name: AMG Capital Management, LLC v. FTC
593 U.S. 67.source: Supreme Court of the United States
593 U.S. 67.excerpt: Section 13(b) of the Federal Trade Commission Act does not authorize the Commission to seek, or a court to award, equitable monetary relief such as restitution or disgorgement.

593 U.S. 83.name: Carr v. Saul
593 U.S. 83.source: Supreme Court of the United States
593 U.S. 83.excerpt: Principles of issue-exhaustion do not require Social Security disability claimants to argue at the agency level that the administrative law judges hearing their disability claims were unconstitutionally appointed.

593 U.S. 98.name: Jones v. Mississippi
593 U.S. 98.source: Supreme Court of the United States
593 U.S. 98.excerpt: A discretionary sentencing system is both constitutionally necessary and constitutionally sufficient to sentence a defendant who committed a homicide when he or she was under 18 to life without parole; a separate factual finding of permanent incorrigibility is not required.

594 U.S. 1.name: United States v. Arthrex, Inc.
594 U.S. 1.source: Supreme Court of the United States
